newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai firm sees U.S. poultry plant ready mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: Thai firm sees U.S. poultry plant ready mid-1998.

text.p: Thailand's agribusiness giant Charoen Pokphand expected its first U.S.-based poultry plant to start operations by mid-1998, a company executive said on Wednesday.
Adirek Sripratak, the president of CP's Agro-Industry Business, told Reuters that the $130-million project was proceeding on schedule.
"The plant will initially process one million chickens a week. And we hope to start operating by mid-1998," he said.
Sources said the company aimed to double the output by the year 2000. The products will be sold locally and exported.
The large size of the U.S. market, cheaper feed ingredients and newly developed technologies were reasons behind CP's decision to set up a plant there, he said.

"We have been leader in this business for 30 years. With our experience, access to lower cost of feed ingredients, and opportunity to acquire new technology, we should do well in the U.S. market," Adirek told Reuters.
